If one tablet contains 500 mg of paracetamol, how many tablets would be needed to obtain one mole of paracetamol?

2. Mercury forms different compounds.

(b)

Mercury vapour is toxic if inhaled.

A person inhales 6 litres of air per minute. The air contains 2.5 × 10−5 ppm of mercury vapour.

Calculate the mass of mercury vapour, in mg, inhaled in 8 hours.

4. A student was investigating the percentage calcium carbonate content of an eggshell.

0.390 g of ground eggshell was placed in a beaker containing 20.0 cm3 of 1.00 mol l−1 hydrochloric acid.

CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(ℓ)

Once the reaction was complete, the solution was quantitatively transferred to a 100 cm3 standard flask and made up to the mark with distilled water.

10.0 cm3 samples of the solution were titrated with 0.100 mol l−1 sodium hydroxide solution. The average titre was 11.65 cm3.

NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H2O(ℓ)

(b)

Using the results obtained by the student, calculate the percentage, by mass, of calcium carbonate present in the eggshell.

3

7. Cisplatin was the first member of a class of platinum-containing anti-cancer drugs.

Clinical use of the drug is now limited since cancer cells can develop resistance to it.

(b)

A new drug being trialled, asplatin, may be capable of overcoming drug resistance in cancer cells.

Asplatin is synthesised by reacting oxoplatin with acetylsalicylic anhydride.

During a trial synthesis, 5.00 g of oxoplatin was reacted with excess acetylsalicylic anhydride to produce 6.36 g of asplatin.

Calculate the percentage yield.

2
